item.title: Localizing Restriction Categories
item.description: arXiv:2610.30553v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The localizing/separating factorization, which is the analogue, for restriction categories, to the surjective/embedding factorization for topoi, is developed at both the mere restriction category and join restriction category level. The factorization system at both the ordinary and join level is approached using the notion of a density, which is a stable and universal suborder of the restriction order. The main technical results of the paper construct the join localization and establish its basic properties. The paper gives several examples of localizations. In particular, examples of localization on commutative rigs are provided which give a way to construct categories of schemes. The Zariski spectrum and the Pierce spectrum are, in particular, developed.
item.dc:creator: Robin Cockett

item.title: The symmetric skew monoidal structure of Gray-categories
item.description: arXiv:2610.31410v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In a previous paper, we constructed a closed skew monoidal structure on the category of Gray-categories and Gray-functors whose internal hom Psd(A, B) captures pseudomaps and pseudo-transformations. In the present paper we give a symmetric description of the Gray-category Psd(A,B) and use this to prove that the skew monoidal structure is symmetric skew monoidal.
item.dc:creator: John Bourke, Gabriele Lobbia

item.title: Semi-strict 4-categories as enriched categories
item.description: arXiv:2610.31448v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We introduce several flavours of semi-strict 4-category as enriched categories. We give the axioms for semi-strict 4-categories in elementary terms and describe a wide range of examples. In particular, we answer the question of what exactly Gray-categories and the higher transformations between them form: namely, a left-sharp 4-category G-Cat$^4$. In addition, we describe examples arising from braided monoidal 2-categories, monoidal Gray-categories (herein defined) and Gray-categories with structure. We use the concepts introduced here and the relationships between them to unify various concepts in the literature, such as Crans' 4-teisi. In the second part of the paper, we investigate homotopical aspects. In particular, we classify the equivalence n-cells in the left-sharp 4-category G-Cat$^4$ for each n. Using this, we show that the left-sharp skew monoidal structure on the category of Gray-categories induces a symmetric monoidal closed structure on the homotopy category of Gray-categories.
item.dc:creator: John Bourke, Gabriele Lobbia

item.title: Properties of theories whose algebras are free
item.description: arXiv:2610.31599v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: A hard theorem of Givant classifies the finitary algebraic theories for which every algebra is free. From it, one easily deduces that all such theories are minimal (adding any further equations makes them trivial) and have a well-defined notion of dimension (free algebras on sets of different cardinality are never isomorphic). We prove both these properties directly, without the aid of Givant's theorem.
item.dc:creator: Tom Leinster, Maia Woolf

item.title: Simple-shifted monoidal derived equivalences for tensor categories
item.description: arXiv:2610.26196v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In this paper, we investigate monoidal derived equivalences between tensor categories with infinitely many isomorphism classes of simple objects. We introduce the notion of a simple-shifted monoidal derived equivalence and prove that a simple-shifted monoidal derived equivalence gives rise to a tensor equivalence. In addition, we investigate which tensor categories have the property that every monoidal derived equivalence between them is necessarily simple-shifted, and we establish some sufficient conditions for this property. As a corollary, we prove that if a tensor category is monoidally derived equivalent to the finite-dimensional representation category of either the quantized enveloping algebra $U_q(\mathfrak{g})$, the quantized Borel subalgebra $U_q^{\geq 0}(\mathfrak{g})$, or the quantized coordinate ring $\mathcal{O}_{q}(G)$ (for a suitable $q$), it is tensor equivalent to the corresponding category.
item.dc:creator: Jing Yu

item.title: Logics vs doctrines, a mirror symmetry
item.description: arXiv:2610.29771v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study the relationship between doctrines, encoding 2-categories of theories in predicate logic, and fragments of geometric logic, defined through Kan injectivity in the 2-category of topoi. After a brief historical account of the notion of doctrine, we propose our working definition. Our main result then establishes a Galois connection between doctrines and subgeometric logics. This connection suggests a mirror symmetry between the world of doctrines and the world of logics, in which constructions and results on either side admit counterparts on the other. We develop this symmetry through constructions of syntactic categories and classifying topoi in both settings, recovering the familiar examples from categorical logic. We prove paired Diaconescu-type theorems and give symmetric universal characterisations of the two closure operators induced by the Galois connection. Finally, we show that passing from a doctrine to its closure induces a reflection between the corresponding 2-categories of algebras, and we relate this reflection to conceptual completeness.
item.dc:creator: Ivan Di Liberti, Umberto Tarantino, Lingyuan Ye

item.title: Restricted (2+1)-TQFTs supported by thickened and solid tori
item.description: arXiv:2505.21373v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: A faithful $(1+1)$ TQFT has recently been constructed, but the existence of a faithful $(2+1)$ TQFT remains an open question, that subsumes the hard problem of linearity of mapping class groups of surfaces. To circumvent the latter problem we construct a subcategory of the category of 3-cobordisms, containing disjoint unions of tori and simplest cobordisms between them. On this we define TQFTs that are able to distinguish pairs of torus bundles and lens spaces, previously shown not to be distinguishable by quantum invariants.
item.dc:creator: Du\v{s}an {\DJ}or{\dj}evi\'c, Danica Kosanovi\'c, Jovana Nikoli\'c, Zoran Petri\'c

item.title: The Game-Theoretic Kat\v{e}tov Order and Idealised Effective Subtoposes
item.description: arXiv:2602.08138v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: This paper addresses the longstanding problem of determining the structure of the $\leq_{\mathrm{LT}}$-order in the Effective Topos, known to effectively embed the Turing degrees. In a surprising discovery, we show that the $\leq_{\mathrm{LT}}$-order is in fact tightly controlled by the combinatorics of filters on $\omega$, raising deep questions about how combinatorial and computable complexity interact, both within this order and beyond it. To make the connection precise, we introduce a game-theoretic (''gamified'') variant of the Kat\v{e}tov order on filters over $\omega$, which turns out to exhibit a striking mix of coarseness and subtlety. For one, it is strictly coarser than the classical Rudin-Keisler order and, when viewed dually on ideals, collapses all MAD families to a single equivalence class. On the other hand, the order also supports a rich internal structure, including an infinite strictly ascending chain of ideal classes, which we identify by way of a new separation technique. From the computability-theoretic perspective, we show that a computable (and extended) variant of the gamified Kat\v{e}tov order is isomorphic to the original $\leq_{\mathrm{LT}}$-order. Moreover, our work brings into focus a new degree-spectrum invariant for filters $\mathcal{F}$, $$\mathcal{D}_{\mathrm{T}}(\mathcal{F}):=\{\,[f\colon\omega\to\omega] \mid f\leq_{\mathrm{LT}} \mathcal{F} \},$$ which is shown to always determine a proper initial segment of the Turing degrees. Extending this, given any non-principal $\Delta^1_1$ filter $\mathcal{F}$, we show that $\mathcal{D}_{\mathrm{T}}(\mathcal{F})$ is precisely the class of hyperarithmetic degrees. This significantly generalises previous results obtained by van Oosten \cite{vO14} and Kihara \cite{Kih23}. The proofs draw on ideas from general topology, descriptive set theory, and computability theory.
item.dc:creator: Takayuki Kihara, Ming Ng

item.title: The shifted symplectic geometry of derived higher groupoids
item.description: arXiv:2607.17362v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: The main goal of this work is to introduce derived Lie n-groupoids and their shifted symplectic structures. We further define shifted lagrangian structures and prove that their composition is well defined under suitable conditions. As an application, we show that our framework incorporates several reduction procedures at critical values, including: classical Hamiltonian reduction, group valued moment maps, Poisson Lie group valued moment maps and Mikami-Weinstein for proper symplectic groupoids.
item.dc:creator: Miquel Cueca, Florian Dorsch, Reyer Sjamaar, Chenchang Zhu
